issues.issue: The preamble names "ICICI BANK LIMITED, New York Branch (or any of its overseas branches or subsidiaries party hereto)" as Escrow Agent and Account Bank, leaving it uncertain which legal entity holds that office. Branches are not separate legal persons, and the parenthetical does not say how or when a subsidiary becomes the acting agent.

The recitals state Project cost as "currently estimated to be approximately" US$1,097,000,000 and financing of US$530,000,000/US$713,000,000, yet operative provisions treat those figures as fixed thresholds (Section 2.08(b) permits commitment reduction only if Project costs fall below US$1,097,000,000, and the Financial Closure definition requires exactly US$530,000,000). A court could be asked whether the recital's estimate controls the operative tests.

The recital states flatly that "This Term Loan Facility is guaranteed in accordance with the terms of the Guarantee Agreements by" the Parent and EGL, whereas the EGL Guarantee Agreement caps EGL's post-Commercial-Operations-Date liability at $250,000,000 and terminates it on the EGL Guarantee Release Date. The recital's unqualified language can be argued against the limited guarantee actually delivered.

The cross-reference is left incomplete — "Section 2.20(b" — so the definition points to a subsection that is not properly identified. The reader must supply the missing closing reference to know which provision assigns the meaning.

"Any material property or assets" fixes no threshold, so it is not determinable when an acquisition creates an Additional Collateral Date and triggers the Section 5.14 security obligations. "Material" is nowhere defined for this purpose.

The closing condition is ungrammatical — "require a mandatory prepayment ... on the same terms as the required by the Loans" — and it is unclear whether it qualifies only clause (b)(iii) or the whole quotient. The defect changes which debt goes into the denominator of the pro rata share.

The definition of "Additional Obligations" is circular: it defines the term as obligations under the Supplier Financing "in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Additional Obligations." The limiting phrase uses the term being defined, so its outer boundary cannot be fixed from the text.

After enumerating supplemental security documents, control agreements and consents, the definition sweeps in "each other security agreement or other security instrument or document executed and delivered to the reasonable satisfaction of the Security Agent." That open catch-all sits against the enumerated specifics and has no stated limit on what the Security Agent may demand.

Clause (1)(A) makes the inclusion of equity in a Person's net income "subject to the limitations contained in clause (4) below," but clause (4) addresses extraordinary, unusual or nonrecurring gains and losses and contains no limitation on equity income. The internal cross-reference does not match the clause it points to.

Item (f) deducts "bad or doubtful expenses not provided for," a phrase that is not an accounting concept (the standard term is bad or doubtful debts). What must be deducted cannot be determined from the words used.

"Agents" is defined to include the Intercreditor Agent, but under the Intercreditor Agent and Intercreditor Agreement definitions that office exists only "if and when appointed" under an intercreditor agreement that may never be entered into. Provisions addressed to the "Agents" collectively are therefore of uncertain application.

Clause (ii) capitalizes leases that are not Capital Lease Obligations, but the closing sentence says "Attributable Debt" excludes ordinary-course operating leases not required by GAAP to be treated as capital leases. The two sentences cannot both be given full effect for an ordinary-course operating lease.

"Borrowing" is defined to include "an LC Exposure," yet Section 2.03(c) requires that "each Borrowing shall be comprised entirely of Eurodollar Rate Borrowings" and Section 2.04 requires every Borrowing to be requested by a Borrowing Request specifying an Interest Period. An LC Exposure cannot satisfy those requirements, so the definition and Section 2.03(c)/2.04 pull apart.

The clause reads "commercial banks in the Hibbing, Minnesota, New York, New York, and Singapore are authorized or required by law to remain closed" — a grammatical failure that leaves it unclear whether closure in any one of the three centres, or all of them, disqualifies the day. The stray article and the plural verb make the list's operation uncertain.

Cash counts only if held at "reputable banks or financial institutions, acceptable to the Lenders," with no standard governing acceptability and no requirement of reasonableness. The parenthetical in clause (c) is also left unclosed, blurring where the Lien carve-out ends.

"Standalone net profits after taxation" is neither defined nor a GAAP line item, although Section 1.03 requires accounting terms to be construed in accordance with GAAP. The starting figure for the DSCR therefore has no fixed content.

The syntax leaves it unclear whether "certificates of deposit or time deposits with a maturity of less than six (6) months, issued by a commercial bank" is a second, independent category or must also be government-issued or guaranteed. The single "and" joining the two limbs can be read either way.

The deduction of "the lesser of actual maintenance capital expenditures and US$12,500,000" states no period for the cap, although the definition applies "for any period" and the sweep is tested quarterly. Whether the $12,500,000 is an annual or a per-quarter limit is not stated.

The definition counts scheduled repayments of the Loans, Supplier Financing and Permitted Capex Additional Indebtedness only, omitting other Additional Indebtedness permitted by Section 6.01. The enumeration invites an expressio unius argument that other permitted debt service never reduces the sweep.

The clause says only that the Lenders and Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors "shall have the right to receive" the sweep amount; it imposes no express payment obligation on the Borrower. Whether the Borrower is bound to pay, and on what demand, must be gathered from elsewhere.

The defining parenthetical is misplaced: "results in an amount (a \"Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount\") in excess of 1.15" attaches the defined term to the ratio rather than to the fifty-percent product, contrary to the parallel placement in clause (i). Read literally the Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount is a DSCR figure, not a dollar amount.

This clause directs that any shortfall in the Sweep Amount be paid "out of cash in the DSRA," which cannot readily be squared with the DSRA definition and Section 5.15, under which the Borrower must maintain the Required Amount as a debt service reserve. Draining the reserve to fund a voluntary-style sweep works against the reserve obligation.

The clause requires retroactive adjustment of the fourth-quarter Sweep Amount but provides only for "adjustment ... in the distributions with respect to the Sweep Amount for the first fiscal quarter," with no mechanism if the audited results show an overpayment exceeding the next quarter's sweep. Whether any refund is owed is not addressed.

The First Sweep Period runs from nine months after the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date to April 1, 2014, but the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date may be as late as June 30, 2013, leaving a period of a day or two (and none at all if that date slips). Read with the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date definition, the First Sweep Period may be empty.

"Each full fiscal quarter during the applicable Sweep Period" is undefined where the Sweep Period begins mid-quarter (nine months after the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date). Whether the partial opening quarter counts is not stated.

Applying this definition, the Sweep Payment Date for one quarter is itself the Sweep Date for the next under the Sweep Date definition, so the same date carries both characters and the sweep is computed a quarter in arrears. The interlock between the two definitions is not made explicit.

The 49% acquisition trigger cannot be squared with the LLC Pledge Agreement and the Pledged Borrower LLC Interests definition, under which 51% of the Borrower's Equity Interests are pledged to the Security Agent for the Secured Parties. Enforcement of that pledge by transfer to a purchaser would itself produce a Change in Control.

"Collateral" is defined as "any and all \"Collateral\", as defined in any applicable Security Document" — a circular reference that pushes the content of the term entirely into other instruments. Its scope cannot be settled from this Agreement.

The Collateral Account Agreement is described as "established for purposes of the DSRA and the Escrow Account," yet the Insurance and Other Proceeds Account definition and the Net Debt definition refer to the Insurance and Other Proceeds Account and the Unrestricted Account as also being established under it. The stated purpose is narrower than the accounts the document is elsewhere said to govern.

The date turns on certification that "commercial production has commenced," a term nowhere defined and set by no output, duration or quality benchmark. Because the guarantee periods and sweep dates run off this date, its trigger is left to the certifier's judgment.

The definition requires notice to and certification by the "Lenders' Engineering Consultant," a capitalized term that is not defined; the Agreement defines only "Engineering Consultant." Whether they are the same person, and who appoints the certifier, is not stated.

Commitment Percentage is measured against the "aggregate Total Commitment," but Total Commitment is defined as a fixed US$250,000,000 (increasable to US$530,000,000) rather than as the sum of the Lenders' actual commitments. If commitments are cancelled under Section 2.08(a), the percentages need not aggregate to 100% for Required Lender votes.
